@graph.title: The root README, and the one fact it must carry
@graph.description: Write the repository's root README when there is none, carrying a link to the harness that was installed and the overall install status. Never replaces one that exists. The last thing initialize-harness does before it ends installed.

@graph.name: bootstrap-graph-emission
@graph.title: Emitting bootstrap's own graph
@graph.description: How bootstrap emits its OWN graph as `.jsonld`/`.json`, and why that emission is the one obligation the layer cannot trade away. bootstrap is exempt from the visualiser requirement every layer above it carries; what it owes instead is this document — in the owner's words, its `.json`/`.jsonld` *"is its existence"*. A layer that cannot emit its own graph has not shown it is a graph.

@graph.name: bootstrap-graph-publication
@graph.title: Publishing bootstrap's graph
@graph.description: Where bootstrap's graph is published, why its `@id` must equal exactly that path, why a `.json` alias sits beside the canonical `.jsonld`, and why the document is NOT committed any more. The failure this skill exists to stop is `blv9` — a self-describing artefact whose own `@id` dereferenced to nothing, for months, while the generator worked perfectly.

@graph.name: initiator
@graph.title: Initiator
@graph.description: An agent being requested to initialize a cat-harness with ONLY the knowledge bootstrap/README.md hands it. That constraint is the role, not a caveat on it: an Initiator has no MCP server, no harness, no work plan and no skills beyond those bootstrap carries, and a step that assumes any of those is a step an Initiator cannot perform. It stops being an Initiator the moment the harness is installed and it re-enters through that harness instead.

@graph.name: knowledge-graph-data-store
@graph.title: Knowledge Graph Data Store
@graph.description: A git repository, reached either through the git CLI or through a forge's API. It is where a declaration and its graph are READ from and where a new instance's declaration is WRITTEN to. It is `actedUpon`: it holds and serves, and takes no part in deciding what should happen — which is why it carries no skills and why naming one for it would be a lie about what it does.

@graph.name: requestor
@graph.title: Requestor
@graph.description: Wants to initialize — or bootstrap, or install, or load, or harness — a harness: bootstrap itself, or a derivative such as cat-harness, folio-assistant or smart-guidelines. Carries no skills deliberately: WHICH harness this repository should become is a judgement about intent, and no instruction body produces it. The Initiator may narrow the list from context; only the Requestor settles it.

@graph.name: logger
@graph.title: Logger
@graph.description: A machine that accepts log messages and puts them somewhere a person can read. Like the Knowledge Graph Data Store it is `actedUpon` — it receives and records, takes no part in what happens next, and carries no skills, because the skill belongs to whoever is DOING the thing being logged. The Logger is not the author of a log line; it is where the line goes. That distinction is why `log-message` takes `actor` as a required input: the Logger cannot infer who acted, and a log that names the logger rather than the actor records nothing worth having.

@graph.name: schemas
@graph.description: The two JSON Schema documents the discussion process is checked against — `discussion.input.schema.json` (what is known before asking) and `discussion.output.schema.json` (what the exchange determined). MOVED OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21: a schema is not an instruction body, and while they sat among the `.md` a consumer asking this instance for its schemas was told it has none. This directory was deliberately NOT created when the rest of the layout was split, because declaring a directory that does not exist is the `dh4f` defect — the files had to move first. Their published `$id`s are UNCHANGED and still read `/bootstrap/skills/discussion/`: `gen-bootstrap-schemas.ts` calls that half of a contract cited from five languages' catalogues, and ids are stable across a relocation while paths are not. `graphKinds: ["schemas"]` alone, matching `bootstrap-tools`'s self-declaration of its own `schemas/`; the `["schemas", "cat-harness"]` pairing is how the ROOT declares somebody else's.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.description: CatBootstrap's three Roles — Initiator, Knowledge Graph Data Store, and the person asking. Declared as `scenarios` on 2026-09-21, matching `cat-harness/scenarios/`: before the split this inherited `skills` from the directory above it, so a consumer asking for the Scenarios got skill bodies and a consumer asking for Skills got a role registry. A lane name is a string the audit cannot bind to anything, which is why these Roles were declared at all rather than left implicit in the diagrams' lanes. RENAMED from `bootstrap-roles` on 2026-09-21: `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES` carries `scenarios` as the convention, and overrides match on ID, so a qualified id did not override the default — it ADDED a second entry at the same path and this directory resolved TWICE. The same defect was fixed in `cat-harness/cat-harness.json` and missed here. The id had to differ from `cat-harness`, which `skills/` holds; `scenarios` was always free.

@graph.name: processes
@graph.description: The bootstrap PROCESSES — `initialize-harness.bpmn`, the one an actor starts, and `log-message.bpmn`, an independent sub-process any step may call. Declared because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree: until 2026-09-19 `findBpmnDirs` found this directory by WALKING from the repository root, which also walked it into folio-assistant's graph (88 references to `Process_CatBootstrap` in `_kg/folio-assistant.jsonld`, measured). A separate id from `cat-harness`, because overrides match on id and `skills/` already holds that one — reusing it would replace bootstrap's skills with its workflows. RENAMED from `bootstrap-processes` on 2026-09-21: `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES` carries `processes` as the convention, and overrides match on ID, so a qualified id did not override the default — it ADDED a second entry at the same path and this directory resolved TWICE. The same defect was fixed in `cat-harness/cat-harness.json` and missed here. The id had to differ from `cat-harness`, which `skills/` holds; `processes` was always free.

@graph.name: models
@graph.description: Which languages a model is good at, and whether anybody checked. In BOOTSTRAP for the reason everything else here is: an agent reaching for the language it should communicate in has not yet loaded the harness that would otherwise answer, so a registry one layer up would be unreachable in exactly the case it exists for. `context`: read when a session opens, never written by a process — a person grants a validation, an agent never does, because a model's own claim about its languages is the thing the validation state exists to distrust.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.description: The swimlane glossary's retirement ledger. Declared rather than hidden because a consumer must be able to find what this instance has ever called a term: the glossary document is regenerated from the corpus each run and has no memory, so the one fact that cannot be re-derived — that a concept was once minted — is committed here. Keyed by the IRI's local part, never the absolute IRI, because the publication base is a deploy-time variable and a stored absolute IRI would rot the day it moved.

@graph.name: bootstrap-translations
@graph.description: The gettext templates for THIS instance's workflow diagrams — one directory per target locale, holding the `.pot` extracted from each `.bpmn` here. Undeclared until 2026-09-22, and that was the `dh4f` defect: `j28g` moved these out of `cat-harness/translations/` correctly, because the templates belong beside the instance that owns the diagrams, and the declaration did not follow. Fifteen committed files a consumer scanning the declared set would report a clean run over. A SEPARATE id from cat-harness's `translation-sources`: overrides match on id, so reusing it would REPLACE that graph with this one rather than add to it. `reproduce` for the reason cat-harness's entry gives — a downstream instance translating this diagram set needs catalogues of its own, not a pointer to these. Bean `m9zz`.

@graph.name: agent-instructions
@graph.title: AGENTS.md — bootstrap
@graph.description: Phase one of two. Valid with nothing installed: no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no beans. The default behaviour of initialisation is to copy this file, and the last bootstrap step re-enters through the installed harness, which is what supplies phase two. No `source` because this is the origin — an absent source means authored here, which is a different fact from an upstream that cannot be reached.
